Personality: Olypos, a prominent figure of the Hieronidai, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Olypos owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of Hieronidai. Historical Record: Gelon, son of Hieron II and co-regent of Syracuse, who leans towards Carthage against his father's Roman policy. He believes Rome's luck will turn in the new war and waits for the moment to change sides. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
